Karthik: Heads-up: a customer reported missing audit fields when exporting to Splunk via S3 with KMS encryption. Anyone seen this pattern?

Emma: Which fields are missing? do we have a sample object?

Karthik: They said actor.ip and resource.id are absent in the exported object. In the hosted UI logs the fields are present. Suspect something in the export pipeline or our schema transform when writing to S3 (maybe happens before/after KMS envelope encrypt).

Jules: S3 export flow is: write newline-delimited JSON -> gzip -> multipart upload -> (if enabled) envelope-encrypt using KMS -> finalize. KMS shouldn't mutate the payload. My first guess is a schema-version-transform step running for older customers.

Li: Also note: Splunk customers often map fields to ECS names. If their pipeline expects source.ip or client.ip and we emit actor.ip, it may look "missing". worth confirming exact raw object bytes vs what splunk parsed.

Karthik: Agreed. Customer pasted this snippet from their Splunk ingest showing empty actor.ip. I'll paste a minimal example of what we expect vs what they saw:

```
EXPECTED (canonical): {"ts":"2026-03-12T17:22:10Z","actor":{"id":"u-123","ip":"18.7.9.10"},"resource":{"id":"r-456","type":"model"},"action":"deploy"}

THEIR EXPORT: {"ts":"2026-03-12T17:22:10Z","actor":{},"resource":{"type":"model"},"action":"deploy"}
```

Emma: If raw S3 object contains the expected JSON then it's a downstream mapping issue. If raw object already missing fields, pipeline bug. We need a quick validation check we can run for onboarding customers.

Jules: I can add a small verifier that downloads an example object, runs KMS decrypt (using customer CMK or our test key), and validates against the canonical audit schema (json-schema). Returns a short report: present/missing fields + suggestions.

Karthik: Perfect. Let's also expose a "validate-export" endpoint for onboarding: POST a sample S3 object URL (pre-signed), or POST webhook sample payload. Endpoint returns mapping suggestions for Splunk/Datadog/SIEM and flags if KMS envelope metadata missing.

Li: Security note: verifier MUST NOT log plaintext audit events. Only emit a hashed fingerprint and field-presence booleans. Also rotate any temporary keys used to fetch objects. Don't keep decrypted copies.

audit-bot: Created ticket SEC-742: audit-export-validation endpoint + schema compatibility report (assignee: Jules).

Jules: Will implement lambda + small CLI wrapper. Plan: fetch -> decrypt via KMS (assume role) -> validate json-schema v2 -> run mapping heuristics for ECS/CEF -> return JSON report. ETA: EOD next Tue.

Emma: I'll draft onboarding docs and include Splunk transforms.conf snippet mapping actor.ip -> source.ip and resource.id -> target.id, plus a Datadog pipeline example. Also add a sample terraform snippet for granting read/decrypt ACLs to the verifier role.

Karthik: On schema side: propose we bump audit-schema to 2.1 with explicit deprecations and an opt-in compatibility toggle for Dedicated/Private. Add a migration guide for customers who rely on older fields.

Li: Also add a test case in infra CI that simulates multipart upload + envelope encrypt + validator roundtrip. Catch regressions in export transforms.

Emma: One more onboarding suggestion: provide a small curl-based verification customers can run before we onboard them:

```
curl -X POST https://onboard.redwood.ai/validate-export \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"s3_presigned_url":"https://...","type":"s3"}'
```

Karthik: Nice. Action items:
- Jules: build validator lambda + CLI (SEC-742) ✅
- Emma: docs + transforms templates + terraform snippet
- Karthik: draft schema bump PR + release note
- Li: add CI test and ensure logs never contain plaintext

Jules: I'll open the PRs and link to SEC-742. ping me if you want to see a quick demo when ready. :thumbsup:

Li: +1. I'll run a quick scan for any existing export transforms that might drop keys.

audit-bot: SEC-742 status: in progress. Comments: "remember to mask PII in validator responses".
